DATASET_COVERAGE_MAP.note: Non-PII per-source coverage snapshot published to public IPFS (dataset-coverage.json). Set as a Vercel Production environment variable. The value is a public content identifier (CID); no secret is stored here. getOracleDatasetInfo merges this on top of the server's built-in coverage defaults (lee, miami-dade, orange, palm-beach).

PROPERTY_QUERY_TABLE_MAP.note: The per-property query table carries owner PII and was NOT published to public IPFS (dry-run only; see docs/decisions/ipfs-publication.md sections 2, 5, 6). The CID above is the dry-run content address and is intentionally not resolvable on a public gateway. It is recorded here as the wiring target that activates once a redacted, eligible table is published. It is deliberately NOT set in the live deployment: getOracleDatasetInfo opens a DuckDB view over the property query table when a county is present in this map, so pointing it at an unreachable CID makes the dataset-info call fail and suppresses the county's coverage. With this map left unset for duval, queryProperties returns no rows for duval (the county is not served by a property query table) — the intended behaviour per the decision record.
